statements.attributed: uses a dense metallic film to reduce the IR thermal loss, but its poor breathability limits daily wearing
statements.quote: For instance, the commercially available Mylar blanket uses a dense metallic film to reduce the IR thermal loss, but its poor breathability limits daily wearing. Several attempts have been made to develop low‐emissivity textiles with improved breathability, which potentially reduce indoor environment set‐points and save building heating energy.[ , , ]

statements.attributed: demonstrates that the human body dissipates heat to the cold outer space through an atmospheric window
statements.quote: The presence of an atmospheric window (8–13 µm), which corresponds to the peak wavelength (9.7 µm) of human body radiation at 33 °C (Figure 1c), allows the human body dissipates heat to the cold outer space (T = 2.7 K), leading to enhanced radiative loss. Moreover, the increased convective heat coefficient in the outdoor environment poses another challenge to maintain our thermal comfort. Fortunately, if outdoor solar irradiation can be efficiently harvested by textiles, it is possible to realize effective personal warming in a green manner.

statements.attributed: uses expensive conductive fabrics or nanoporous polyethylene textiles, limiting large-scale applications
statements.quote: Moreover, most previous radiative warming textiles are made from expensive conductive fabrics or nanoporous polyethylene (Nano‐PE) textiles. As a result, large‐scale applications are currently not feasible.

statements.attributed: demonstrates that the solar absorptances of plasmonic metamaterials are notably reduced when coated on nylon 66 porous films and cottons compared to flat metal substrates
statements.quote: For instance, Li et al. and Zhang et al. demonstrated that the solar absorptances of their plasmonic metamaterials are notably reduced when coated on nylon 66 porous films (from 95% to 45%) and cottons (from 95% to 83.7%) compared to flat metal substrates. Alternatively, Wang et al. demonstrated that the solar absorptance of their MoO x ‐based multilayer SSFs show a notable decrease from 93% to 83% when coated on cotton compared to flat metal films. To address this commonplace and critical issue, for the first time, we resorted to high‐entropy strategies in the development of SSFs for textiles

statements.attributed: high-entropy nitride is a category of up-and-coming photothermal materials due to its unique and fascinating structural characteristics, and large compositional space
statements.quote: High‐entropy nitride is a category of up‐and‐coming photothermal materials due to its unique and fascinating structural characteristics, and large compositional space.[ , , ] It remains, however, a significant challenge to achieve desired spectral selectivity on rough and porous substrates.

statements.attributed: used as a reference for the optical constants of the SS substrate and Si3N4 film
statements.quote: The optical constants of the SS substrate and Si3N4 film were referred to our previous work. According to the optimized parameters such as the N2 flow rate and layer thickness, a triple‐layer SSF was successfully fabricated, which shows a high solar absorptance of 96.2% and suppressed thermal emittance of 8.8%.

statements.attributed: demonstrates that high-entropy materials composed of transition metals have enhanced d electron intensities around the Fermi level and narrow bandgaps
statements.quote: For high‐entropy materials composed of transition metals, the d electron intensities around the Fermi level are enhanced compared with the low‐entropy counterparts; besides, high‐entropy nitrides composed of transition metals have narrow bandgaps. Therefore, d‐d transitions are easily activated, that is, the d‐band electrons with energy above the bandgap transit from the valence band to the conduction band, thereby enhancing solar harvesting capability in the UV–vis–NIR region. Such d‐d band transition induced solar absorption is intrinsic and roughness‐insensitive.

statements.quote: For the Al 2p spectrum (Figure 2e), the peaks at 71.4, 73.7, and 74.1 eV are associated with Al0, Al nitridation, and Al oxidation states, respectively; in addition, no metallic Al is observed for LMVF.

statements.attributed: demonstrates that the porous structures form a continuous refractive index gradient between air and medium, which decreases the IR reflection effectively
statements.quote: On the other hand, at the IR wavelengths regime, the porous structures form a continuous refractive index gradient between air and medium, which decreases the IR reflection effectively. As a result, the resulting textile has significantly increased thermal emittance compared with that on rigid SS substrate. Figure 3b shows an amplifying region and the corresponding elemental mappings, from which each element is homogeneously distributed.

statements.attributed: used as a reference for depositing the well-designed SSF on an Al-decorated Nano-PE
statements.quote: Furthermore, to broaden the working scenarios (e.g., outdoors on cloudy days or at night), we deposited the well‐designed SSF on an Al‐decorated Nano‐PE. Benefitting from the relatively smooth surface, the low thermal emittance of 15.6% and high absorptance of 94.1% are enabled simultaneously, as shown in Figure S27 (Supporting Information), both of which are better than those on common cotton.
